formulas.name: Fully loaded CAC
formulas.definition: All acquisition cost in a period divided by new paying customers in that period: CAC = (media + sales and marketing salaries and headcount costs + tools, agencies and creative + other programme costs) / new_customers. Segment CAC needs explicit, consistent allocation rules.
formulas.climbos_current: shared/growth/calc.ts:34-40 cacFull = (spend + hours × hourlyCost + other) / customers. shared/agents/economics.ts:199-203 calls it with spend over the horizon, owner hours × owner hour value ($50 default, economics.ts:83-88) and other = 0 (economics.ts:203).
formulas.gap: Matches on headcount: owner time counts as labour, consistent with Skok's no-exclusions rule. Differs because other is hard-coded to 0 (economics.ts:203). Tools, agency or freelance help, creative, list or data purchases and ClimbOS's own subscription and credits are dropped, so CAC is understated against Skok's definition. Media-only CAC (calc.ts:28-32) exists but is not shown next to the full figure.

formulas.name: Months to recover CAC (simple)
formulas.definition: CAC / new-customer MRR (ARPA). This is the form behind the 2011 '<12 months' rule; it ignores gross margin and churn.
formulas.climbos_current: Not used as a headline. paybackSimple exists in calc.ts:56-60 but takes contribution, not revenue.
formulas.gap: None needed. ClimbOS should not use the revenue-only form; Skok himself prefers the gross-margin version.

formulas.name: Months to recover CAC (gross-margin adjusted)
formulas.definition: CAC / (ARPA × GM%). The author's 'fully accurate' version. Recovery is per surviving customer and ignores churn.
formulas.climbos_current: Contribution per month = revenue × grossMargin (calc.ts:43-46; economics.ts:132-137) is used, so ClimbOS is gross-margin adjusted. paybackSimple (calc.ts:56-60) is this formula but is not called by playMaths.
formulas.gap: Matches on gross margin. ClimbOS goes further by adding churn (DS-FX4). Its payback is therefore longer than Skok's for the same inputs, and Skok's benchmarks, calibrated on this no-churn form, must not be applied to the ClimbOS number unlabelled.

formulas.name: Churn-weighted (expected) payback — ClimbOS extension, not Skok
formulas.definition: Find the smallest n where Σ_{t=0}^{n-1} cm·(1−c)^t ≥ CAC. Closed form: n = ln(1 − CAC·c/cm) / ln(1 − c). It never pays back if CAC·c/cm ≥ 1.
formulas.source_ref: interpretation building on DS-02-F1 (exponential decay) and DS-07-F1 (cumulative recovery)
formulas.climbos_current: shared/growth/calc.ts:62-71 paybackWithChurn, used at economics.ts:217. The verdict is profitable = CAC ≤ contribution over 12 months (economics.ts:207, 219; horizon economics.ts:89-90).
formulas.gap: Internally consistent with contributionOver (calc.ts:48-54). It counts the month-0 contribution in full, an assumption that payment arrives in the acquisition month. Stricter than Skok's payback. The locked-numbers line (economics.ts:312-313) should say 'with churn' so it is not compared with '<12 months' benchmarks.

formulas.name: Average customer lifetime
formulas.definition: lifetime = 1 / c, where c is the constant churn per period.
formulas.climbos_current: calc.ts:104-108 churnFromLifetime = 1 / months, used by economics.ts:126-130 for older plans.
formulas.gap: Matches, including the constant-churn assumption, which Skok flags as often wrong (DS-03-F5).

formulas.name: Simple LTV
formulas.definition: LTV = ARPA × GM% / c, with the same period for ARPA and c.
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed. ClimbOS uses 12-month churn-weighted contribution instead (customerValue, economics.ts:139-142; contributionOver calc.ts:48-54).
formulas.gap: Deliberate and consistent with Skok's own DCF critique (DS-03-F1) and Book 01 §7 (docs/growth-intelligence/books/01_business_strategy_economics.md:84-88). Do not add an uncapped LTV.

formulas.name: Expansion LTV (constant monthly ARPA growth)
formulas.definition: Inputs: a = initial monthly ARPA × GM, m = monthly dollar ARPA growth × GM, c = monthly customer churn. The widely cited closed form is LTV = a/c + m/c². The image was not verified in this session.
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed. Economics has no expansion field (economics.ts:44-74).
formulas.gap: ClimbOS cannot represent expansion or negative churn, so it understates value for upsell-heavy businesses. A capped-horizon version is proposed in DS-EX4.

formulas.name: DCF LTV
formulas.definition: LTV = Σ_t GP_t × S_t / (1+r)^t + residual, where S_t is survival, GP_t is gross profit per surviving customer including expansion, and r is the discount rate (10% default suggested in 2016).
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed; there is no discounting.
formulas.gap: Over a 12-month horizon, discounting at 10% a year changes value by under about 5%, so it is immaterial. Add it only if the horizon goes past 24 months.

formulas.name: LTV:CAC
formulas.definition: LTV / CAC. The guideline of above 3 assumes simple LTV without GM and GM ≥ 80%.
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed. The test is CAC ≤ 12-month value (economics.ts:219).
formulas.gap: Do not import 3×. It assumes lifetime revenue at GM ≥ 80%, while ClimbOS uses 12-month contribution, so the bases differ.

formulas.name: Customer, revenue and net revenue churn
formulas.definition: customer churn = lost customers / customers at start. MRR churn = MRR lost from churned and downgraded customers / MRR at start. Expansion = expansion MRR / MRR at start. Net MRR churn = MRR churn − expansion; below 0 means negative churn.
formulas.climbos_current: One field, monthlyChurn, described as the 'share of customers lost each month' (economics.ts:48-49; question at economics.ts:382). It is multiplied into revenue value (calc.ts:48-54) and into base losses for goals (shared/agents/goal.ts:71).
formulas.gap: Logo churn is applied to revenue. When small customers churn more, ClimbOS understates value; when large ones churn more, it overstates. Use revenue churn net of expansion for value and payback, and customer churn for customer-count goals (goal.ts:71).

formulas.name: Net revenue retention (NRR)
formulas.definition: NRR = (cohort MRR at start − churned − contraction + expansion) / cohort MRR at start, measured over a year or a month.
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed. shared/attribution/cohorts.ts:19-28 stores revenueMinor per cohort month, so the data exists.
formulas.gap: Derive monthly NRR from cohorts.ts revenue rows.

formulas.name: MRR roll-forward / Net New MRR
formulas.definition: MRR_t = MRR_{t−1} + new + expansion − churned. Net New MRR = new + expansion − churned.
formulas.climbos_current: calc.ts:90-94 nextMrr = MRR × (1 − churn) + new × price. It has no expansion term and is not used by economics.ts.

formulas.name: Sales efficiency to payback
formulas.definition: SE = new ARR in the quarter / S&M spend in the prior quarter. Months to recover CAC ≈ 12 / SE, or 12 / (SE × GM) with gross margin.
formulas.gap: Useful for an observed, company-level check once billing and spend are connected. The lag (prior-period spend) matters for sales-led businesses. Book 12 (docs/growth-intelligence/books/12_analytics_forecasting_pricing.md:105) states the lag principle; the code does not apply it.

formulas.name: Steady-state MRR ceiling (interpretation)
formulas.definition: Growth stops where churned MRR equals new MRR: MRR_max = new MRR per month / monthly revenue churn. With net churn ≤ 0 there is no ceiling.
formulas.source_ref: interpretation of DS-06-F1; Skok shows this by simulation, not as an equation
formulas.gap: A cheap, explainable 'growth ceiling' line for recurring businesses.

formulas.name: Funnel media CAC and break-even cost per click
formulas.definition: Media CAC = CPC / Π(step rates). Break-even CPC = allowable CAC × Π(step rates).
formulas.climbos_current: calc.ts:78-88 breakevenCpc and breakevenPerReach. breakevenPerReach is used at economics.ts:218.
formulas.gap: Matches. ClimbOS uses 12-month churn-weighted value as the allowable CAC.

formulas.name: Subscription cash trough
formulas.definition: Cumulative cash_M = Σ_{m=1}^{M} [contribution received in month m − acquisition spend in month m]. The trough is min_M of cumulative cash, and cash breakeven is the first M where cumulative cash ≥ 0.
formulas.climbos_current: Not computed. lockedNumbers (economics.ts:298-319) reports cost and payback but no lowest cash point. Book 12 asks for it (12_analytics_forecasting_pricing.md:141), as does Book 01 (01_business_strategy_economics.md:96).
formulas.gap: Missing. Owners of small businesses fund the trough themselves.

formulas.name: CAC-aware minimum price (proposed)
formulas.definition: The lowest monthly price whose churn-weighted contribution over H months covers CAC: P_min = CAC × c / (GM × (1 − (1−c)^H)), or CAC / (GM × H) when c = 0.
formulas.source_ref: interpretation of DS-05-F2 (price must cover sales complexity) using DS-FX4
formulas.climbos_current: shared/analysis/decisions.ts:53-67 priceFloor = unitCost / (1 − targetMargin) covers delivery cost only. decisions.ts:33-51 margin excludes acquisition (it says so at :47).
formulas.gap: There is no floor that includes acquisition. Static price-fit thresholds (shared/acquisition/scoring.ts:109 LOW_TICKET_USD_MONTH = 25; shared/agents/capacity.ts:14,55 '$300+ 12-month gross profit') stand in for it. They are not Skok-derived: Skok gives no numeric price lines.

steps: For one customer cohort a month, net cash in month m = −600N + 80N(m − 1), and cumulative cash after M months = N × [−600M + 40M(M − 1)].
Monthly net cash turns positive when 80(m − 1) > 600, i.e. m − 1 ≥ 8, so m = 9.
Trough at M = 8: −600 × 8 + 40 × 8 × 7 = −4,800 + 2,240 = −2,560 per unit of N, so with N = 10 the trough is −25,600.
Doubling growth to N = 20 doubles the trough to −51,200, with the same month-16 breakeven (DS-01-F9).

If each customer prepaid 12 months of contribution (960) in the acquisition month, then 960 − 600 = +360 per customer and there is no trough (DS-01-F8). This assumes a delivery obligation that is ignored here.
